name: The Cult
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Ian Astbury and Billy Duffy started out as goths in feathers and a white Gretsch, got the wrong producer for their biggest song, then let Rick Rubin tell them to plug a Les Paul into a Marshall and turn into a hard rock band. They have been arguing with their own past, mostly happily, ever since.

hero.by: The Cult live, November 2010. Photo: Ted Van Pelt, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A Manchester punk meets a Bradford mystic
eras.text: Billy Duffy came out of the Manchester punk scene that also produced Morrissey and Johnny Marr; Ian Astbury had spent his teens in Hamilton, Ontario and came back to England fixated on Native American culture. Astbury's first band, Southern Death Cult, drew crowds in the north. He walked away from it to start again with Duffy.

q: I think I was put there to get him on the stage
years.src: Billy Duffy: Me, Morrissey & Manchester · Morrissey-solo Wiki
years.h: Duffy joins the Nosebleeds and talks Morrissey into singing
years.p: Billy Duffy replaced Vini Reilly in the Wythenshawe punk band the Nosebleeds, and Steven Morrissey replaced singer Ed Banger. The new line-up played two gigs.
years.xp:
At the second show, at the Ritz, Morrissey threw sweets into the crowd during a song called 'Peppermint Heaven'. Duffy says that was "the first time I thought that he had something special."

Duffy left for Studio Sweethearts, which offered a London flat and a record deal. Looking back on his site, he says he was put there to get Morrissey on stage and to introduce him to [[Johnny Marr|ff621094-2a76-401f-8398-b75b5fd2be24]], a kid three or four years younger in the same circle.

years.cap: Duffy on stage with Theatre of Hate, 1981
years.h: Duffy plays lead in Theatre of Hate, with Mick Jones producing
years.p: Duffy is the guitarist on Theatre of Hate's 1981 album Westworld, produced by [[Mick Jones|01f8343c-06e2-4f05-a137-f8ea7efa85c4]] of [[The Clash|8f92558c-2baa-4758-8c38-615519e9deda]], and plays the Futurama festival alongside [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] and [[The Sisters of Mercy|553d8166-27b0-49fe-b8e4-89a984e2c375]].

years.h: Southern Death Cult signs to Situation Two and cuts 'Moya'
years.p: The band, which played its first show at Queen's Hall, Bradford, in October 1981, signs to the Beggars Banquet imprint. On tour it opens for [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] and Theatre of Hate.
years.xp: Astbury sang, with Buzz Burrows on guitar, Barry Jepson on bass and Aky Qureshi on drums. The name borrowed an old term for the mound-building cultures of the American Southeast, and was also a dig at England's north-south divide.

years.h: Astbury ends Southern Death Cult after a Manchester show
years.p: Sixteen months in, Astbury walks. The band's only album comes out later that year on Beggars Banquet, after the band is gone.

years.cap: Death Cult live in London, September 1983
years.h: Astbury and Duffy start Death Cult
years.p: Astbury and Duffy bring in [[Jamie Stewart|969f20f9-1d0a-4067-b2a0-25061ebda7b3]] on bass and Ray Mondo on drums. The first gig is in Oslo on July 25, and the Death Cult EP comes out the same month.

years.cap: Death Cult press photo with Preston in the line-up, 1983
years.src: Wikipedia: The Cult · Wikipedia: Nigel Preston
years.h: Nigel Preston takes the drum stool from Ray Mondo
years.p: [[Nigel Preston|f31ae14d-b6a3-41cf-ae98-d46da77f1939]] comes over from Sex Gang Children. 'Gods Zoo' follows in October.

eras.title: Dropping the Death
eras.text: In January 1984 the band cut its name to the Cult, partly to shake the goth tag. Within eighteen months it had a Top 40 hit built on a white Gretsch White Falcon, and a second album that sold, by the band's Wikipedia count, about 2.5 million copies.

years.cap: Duffy and Astbury at Eel Pie Studio, 1984
years.src: Wikipedia: The Cult · Wikipedia: Billy Duffy · Louder: She Sells Sanctuary
years.h: 'Spiritwalker' goes to No. 1 on the UK indie chart
years.p: Duffy runs his White Falcon through a flanger for the sound that becomes his signature. The bassline Astbury later reworks for 'She Sells Sanctuary' starts here.

years.h: Dreamtime is cut at Rockfield in Wales
years.p: Produced by John Brand and Joe Julian, the debut reaches No. 21 in the UK. On the tour that follows, the band starts playing a new song called 'She Sells Sanctuary'.

years.src: Guitar Player · Louder: She Sells Sanctuary
years.h: A note for "Steve" gets them Wham!'s producer
years.p: The band wanted Steve Lillywhite and ended up with Steve Brown. 'She Sells Sanctuary', cut at Olympic in March, reaches No. 15 and puts the Cult on Top of the Pops for the first time.
years.xp:
"We got the wrong producer!" Duffy told Guitar Player. A message for "Steve" was taken to mean Brown, who had produced Wham!; his engineering on Thin Lizzy and Sensational Alex Harvey Band records persuaded them to stay. Brown suggested the acoustic chord that kicks off the track.

Duffy played the White Falcon through two Boss delays and a Roland JC-120. Louder says the bowed intro came from a violin bow found in the studio, a nod to Jimmy Page. In March 2023 the song went platinum in the UK.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nigel Preston · Louder: She Sells Sanctuary
years.h: Nigel Preston is fired after the single takes off
years.p: Wikipedia says Preston refused to go on wages once the song was a hit, and the band saw him as unreliable because of drug use. Louder says he was fired for missing the video shoot.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love (The Cult album) · Louder: She Sells Sanctuary
years.h: Love hits No. 4 with a Big Country drummer
years.p: Big Country's Mark Brzezicki plays most of the album; Preston is still on three tracks. 'Rain' and 'Revolution' follow as singles.
years.xp:
Steve Brown produced Love at Jacob's Studios in Farnham and at Olympic over July and August. It went gold in the UK and double platinum in Canada.

Astbury told Louder the rule for the era was to stay away from long hair and guitar solos. That rule lasted about a year.

years.cap: Duffy and Astbury on stage with the Cult, 1985
years.h: Les Warner takes the drums for the world tour
years.p: [[Les Warner|5304293c-5b71-48aa-942f-11017f168754]], who had played with Julian Lennon and Johnny Thunders, drums on the tour that runs into June 1986.

eras.title: A Les Paul, a Marshall, off you go
eras.text: The Cult threw away a finished album, flew to New York and let a young producer named Rick Rubin strip them down to riffs. Electric was the result, and the band followed the sound to Los Angeles, where it got bigger and louder still.

years.h: The band scraps Peace, recorded at the Manor
years.p: Sessions with Steve Brown at the Manor in Oxfordshire produced a whole album. Astbury hated the result and the band went looking for Rick Rubin to remix it.
years.xp:
"We spent a quarter of a million pounds making an album that sounded like soup," Astbury said, as quoted on Wikipedia.

Duffy told the Rockenteurs podcast that Rubin was hired to remix, then negotiated to recut one song from scratch, and the band ended up taking the album apart on the spot. Peace finally came out whole in 2000, as disc three of the Rare Cult box.

years.cap: The Cult backstage on the US Electric tour, 1987
years.src: Wikipedia: Electric · Ultimate Classic Rock · Guitar.com
years.h: Rubin takes away the Gretsch, and Electric goes to No. 4
years.p: Rubin tells Duffy to bin the echo and play a Les Paul through a Marshall, and shows Astbury a VHS of Blue Cheer. Electric makes No. 4 in the UK and No. 38 in the US.
years.xp:
Astbury recalls Rubin's pitch: "Do you guys wanna make English pussy music, or do you want to rock?" Engineer Tony Platt says Rubin wanted the guitars of Back in Black, the drums of Highway to Hell and a Led Zeppelin vocal.

Duffy, on the Rockenteurs podcast, called the switch "quite traumatic". Only a wah-wah pedal was allowed. Andy Wallace engineered, and George Drakoulias was in the room.

years.cap: Duffy and Jamie Stewart in the spotlight, Houston, 1987
years.h: Guns N' Roses opens the American dates
years.p: [[Guns N' Roses|eeb1195b-f213-4ce1-b28c-8565211f8e43]] supports the Cult in the US that year. In Australia the band wrecks £30,000 of equipment, and Japan is called off when nobody will rent them gear.

years.h: Les Warner and the managers are fired after the tour
years.p: Warner sued, more than once, for wrongful dismissal and unpaid royalties on Electric. Astbury, Duffy and Stewart moved to Los Angeles.

years.cap: Duffy in the studio in Vancouver, 1988
years.h: Bob Rock and a session drummer in Vancouver
years.p: Sonic Temple is cut at Little Mountain Sound with Bob Rock, his first album with the band. Mickey Curry plays drums after demos with Eric Singer and Chris Taylor don't work out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sonic Temple · Wikipedia: The Cult
years.h: Sonic Temple goes Top 10 in the US and No. 3 at home
years.p: 'Fire Woman' leads the way and the album goes platinum in America. [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]] sings backing vocals on 'New York City'.
years.xp:
Duffy described it as "rock music from a European perspective with the sensibilities of punk." John Leland called it the Cult's most conventional album and its most convincing.

The band toured Europe with [[Aerosmith|3d2b98e5-556f-4451-a3ff-c50ea18d57cb]] and the US with [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]].

years.cap: Astbury and Duffy, Sonic Temple press photo, 1989
years.src: Wikipedia: Matt Sorum · Ultimate Classic Rock: Matt Sorum
years.h: Slash watches Matt Sorum drum for the Cult and takes him
years.p: [[Matt Sorum|21176a1c-bdbf-43d0-aaae-5f2df97b09bd]] plays the Sonic Temple tour. Slash sees him, and in 1990 Sorum replaces Steven Adler in Guns N' Roses.

eras.title: Tribes, a lawsuit and a show in Rio
eras.text: The band that had conquered America started coming apart: Stewart went home to Canada, Sorum went to Guns N' Roses, and Astbury and Duffy made records with hired hands. Astbury organized a festival and wrote his most personal songs before the whole thing stopped mid-tour.

years.h: Astbury's father dies and the tour is cancelled
years.p: His father died of cancer, and the rest of the Sonic Temple tour was called off. Jamie Stewart then retired to Canada.

years.cap: The Cult live, Ceremony-era press photo
years.h: Astbury puts on A Gathering of the Tribes
years.p: The festival runs in Los Angeles and San Francisco with [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]], [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]], Ice-T, Queen Latifah, [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]] and [[The Cramps|96c1edac-1011-4cb8-882c-27248de35071]]. Wikipedia puts attendance at 40,000.

years.h: Ceremony is made by two men and session players
years.p: Bob Rock produces again; Astbury and Duffy rarely record together. The parents of the Native American boy on the cover sue over use of his image.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, the suit claimed exploitation and unauthorized use, and said the boy felt cursed by images of him burning. It held up the album's release in South Korea, Thailand and Turkey.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nigel Preston · Louder: She Sells Sanctuary · Wikipedia: The Cult
years.h: Nigel Preston dies at 28
years.p: The drummer on the band's first records died of a drug overdose, according to Wikipedia; Louder says heroin. The Cult played a memorial warm-up show for him.

years.h: The self-titled album is the one Astbury calls revealing
years.p: Bob Rock produces a fourth time. It reaches No. 21 in the UK and No. 1 in Portugal.
years.xp: Astbury described the songs as "very personal and very revealing". Per Wikipedia, they deal with sexual abuse he suffered at 15, Nigel Preston's death and his years in Glasgow.

years.cap: The Cult in a Sire press photo
years.h: The Cult breaks up after a show in Rio de Janeiro
years.p: The South American tour is cancelled after the Rio date. The band cites unspecified problems on the tour.

eras.title: On ice, off ice
eras.text: Astbury tried a garage band (Holy Barbarians) and a solo record; Duffy formed Coloursound with Mike Peters. Then the two kept getting back together, through a bruising deal with Atlantic, a stint with Astbury singing for the surviving Doors, and a new start on Roadrunner.

years.cap: The Cult live on the 1999 reunion dates
years.h: Back with Sorum, at the Tibetan Freedom Concert
years.p: Astbury and Duffy re-form with Matt Sorum and Martyn LeNoble. The Cult Rising tour includes eight sold-out nights at the House of Blues in Los Angeles.

years.cap: Duffy in a GQ photo shoot, 2001
years.h: Astbury calls the Atlantic years "soul destroying"
years.p: Beyond Good and Evil comes out on Atlantic, and 'Rise' gets to No. 2 at mainstream rock before the label pulls it. Astbury says the label interfered with the lyrics, the cover and the singles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ian Astbury · Wikipedia: The Cult
years.h: Astbury puts the Cult "on ice" and fronts the Doors
years.p: He sings with Ray Manzarek and Robby Krieger as the Doors of the 21st Century until 2007. The project was sued by John Densmore and Jim Morrison's family.

years.h: Killing Joke's Youth produces Born into This
years.p: The band re-formed in 2006 with [[John Tempesta|c616f1c6-e64f-4028-b891-7bfc2f70d58c]], ex-[[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]], on drums. Martin "Youth" Glover produces its first album for Roadrunner, and that summer the Cult opens for [[The Who|9fdaa16b-a6c4-4831-b87c-bc9ca8ce7eaa]] in Europe.

eras.title: Playing the past, writing the next one
eras.text: The Cult started touring its old albums whole, and in between kept making new records, five with Bob Rock in all. By 2023 it was even revisiting Death Cult.

years.cap: The Cult at Sonisphere, Knebworth, July 2009
yt: Love Live at the Royal Albert Hall, October 10, 2009 (fan clip)
years.h: Love played in order, with Stewart back for an encore
years.p: The Love Live tour plays the 1985 album start to finish. At the Royal Albert Hall, Jamie Stewart and Mark Brzezicki join the second encore.

years.h: Choice of Weapon on Cooking Vinyl, with Bob Rock again
years.p: Duffy said signing with the UK label felt like returning to their roots. Earlier that year 'She Sells Sanctuary' turned up in a Budweiser Super Bowl ad.

years.cap: Astbury and Duffy, Hidden City tour, April 2016
years.h: Hidden City closes a trilogy, then Guns N' Roses again
years.p: The album completes the run that began with Born into This. That year the Cult opens for Guns N' Roses on the Not in This Lifetime tour.

years.h: Under the Midnight Sun, cut back at Rockfield
years.p: Producer Tom Dalgety records the band at Rockfield, where Dreamtime was made, with Astbury partly remote during the pandemic. The band tours the UK with Alice Cooper and North America with Black Rebel Motorcycle Club.

years.cap: Jamie Stewart with Death Cult, Birmingham, November 2023
years.h: The Death Cult 8323 tour plays the earliest songs
years.p: Twelve UK dates focus on Death Cult material, plus Southern Death Cult songs and the first two albums.

years.h: Astbury and Duffy step off the road
years.p: The band announces a break from touring for an undetermined time, to write, record and explore projects "that shall be revealed over time."
